$(l)Spell Entity Node$()

Spells in previous chapters are all cast from the player himself — where you stand and where you look is where the spell starts. But sometimes you want a spell to "fly out on its own" and execute only at the moment it hits something far away. The $(9)Spell Entity Node$() was born for this.

It is a $(l)container node$() that can hold an entire sub-spell tree inside. When executed, it pops $(l)a coordinate$() and $(l)a number$() off the stack (in either order), spawns a "spell entity" at the coordinate, and injects the given amount of mana into it.

This entity triggers according to your settings, and executes its inner sub-spell tree once triggered. The mana source of the sub-spell is the entity itself — it consumes the entity's mana, not yours.

$(l)Configuration Screen$()

Middle-click the spell entity node to open its configuration screen, which offers two settings:

$(l)Trigger Mode:$()
·$(9)Delay$(): the entity keeps flying after spawning and triggers when the countdown ends. Enter the waiting tick count in the input box (1 second = 20 ticks).
·$(9)Hit$(): the entity keeps flying until it hits an entity or a block.

$(l)Movement After Trigger:$()
·$(9)Stop in Place$(): the entity stays fixed at the trigger point, acting as a stationary casting source.
·$(9)Keep Flying$(): the entity keeps its original speed and keeps moving after triggering.

Tip: the entity's flight speed is set by external runes (such as $(9)Drive$()); the spell entity node itself does not grant an initial velocity.

$(l)How It Works$()

$(9)Mana Flow:$()
·When the node executes, it charges the given amount of mana from the $(l)current mana source$() (you / scroll / machine, etc.).
·The spawned entity carries this mana.
·Once triggered, the inner sub-spell consumes $(l)the entity's mana$(), not yours.
·When the entity runs out of mana or the sub-spell finishes, the entity dissipates automatically.

$(9)Dissipation and Termination:$()
·When the entity dissipates for any reason, any sub-spell still running inside it is terminated along with it.
·You can also press the default $(9)I$() key to terminate all spells, including the sub-spells inside spell entities.

$(9)Nesting:$()
·A spell entity's inner sub-tree can contain another spell entity node — the inner entity's mana is drawn from the outer entity's mana, supporting multiple levels of nesting.

$(l)Go design your own long-range spells!$()
